clue.text: Look for weapon after getting started

indicators.note: 'after' puts the weapon behind the opening letter in the answer
'getting started' asks for just the start of the word getting, its opening letter

parts.note: a lance is a jousting knight's long spear

explanation.surface: Someone has begun to hunt around for a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick peek or brief glimpse at something is a synonym of a look.

clue.text: Such an eater, I am on drug treatment

indicators.note: treatment suggests the letters of am on drug are processed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient on medication admits being a glutton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' is the speaker: the anagram describes what the eater is, so 'I' links the definition to 'am on drug'.
explanation.definitionFit: A glutton, or a lover of good food, is a hearty eater of this kind.

clue.text: One day last month, became mature

parts.note: one is the article A
ult., short for ultimo, means of last month in formal letters

explanation.surface: Someone reached maturity on a date in the previous month.
explanation.definitionFit: Fully grown or grown-up is the adjective sense shared by both words.

clue.text: Agree lag should get the rope

parts.note: a lag is an old prisoner, a con or convict
a cord is a thin rope

explanation.surface: Consensus that an old jailbird deserves hanging.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to be in harmony or agreement, now rare.

clue.text: Conservative urgency in showing virtue

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative, the British political party
haste is hurry or urgency

explanation.surface: A Tory politician hurries to display moral rectitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pure and sexually abstinent is displaying a virtue in the old moral sense.

clue.text: Hotel eyeing reform of sanitation

parts.note: Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: reform of means the letters of eyeing are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A hotel inspector looking at better cleanliness.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleanliness practices that protect health are what this word denotes.

clue.text: Brief request to work inside

parts.note: a brief is slang for a lawyer; this kind of lawyer solicits clients' instructions and works in an office rather than arguing in the higher courts

explanation.surface: A short appeal to be allowed to work indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' looks like an adjective meaning short; it is the British slang noun for a lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a brief is a lawyer, and this is the office-based branch of the profession.

clue.text: Slip up and trip

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake or slip up

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles and falls over.
explanation.definitionFit: A short journey to do a task, such as a trip to the shops, is this.

clue.text: Might he outgun a French Protestant?

indicators.note: 'Might he' asks what these letters could become if rearranged, an anagram signalled by possibility

explanation.surface: A question whether some man could outshoot a Calvinist from France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might' looks like a noun for strength but works as the anagram signal on HE OUTGUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Reformed Calvinist church in sixteenth and seventeenth century France were given this name.

clue.text: Managed second, even in temporary accommodation, that's clear

indicators.note: 'in' places the managed, second and even pieces inside the shelter

parts.note: a tent is temporary shelter for camping
ran means managed, as in ran a business
par means equal or even, as in on a par

explanation.surface: Coming second, even while living under canvas, is plain enough.
explanation.definitionFit: See-through or obvious is the shared sense of clear here.

clue.text: American lass has metal aplenty

parts.note: gal is an informal, chiefly American word for a girl
ore is rock from which metal is extracted, a common crossword equivalence

explanation.surface: A girl from the States owns plenty of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are postpositive adjectives meaning in abundance, so the swap works after a noun.

clue.text: Leave out nothing in front of American institute

indicators.note: 'in front of' puts the zero before the institute's letters

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Someone skips nothing ahead of a famous US college.
explanation.definitionFit: To skip or exclude something is a direct synonym of leave out.

clue.text: Sort of milky ale sent cop mad

indicators.note: mad describes letters gone wild, so the words ale sent cop are rearranged

explanation.surface: Beer drives a policeman crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: This word describes a milky iridescence like that of the gemstone opal.

clue.text: Burning with emotion, seeing Peruvian ancestry

parts.note: Incan means belonging to the Inca empire of ancient Peru
descent is lineage or ancestry

explanation.surface: An emotional person is moved by discovering roots in Peru.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally glowing with heat, the word is used figuratively for someone fiercely angry or passionate.

clue.text: Openings for keen photographers

parts.note: reads like job vacancies for enthusiastic snappers, but means the adjustable holes in camera lenses that let in light

explanation.surface: Job vacancies advertised for enthusiastic photographers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Openings' suggests job vacancies; it means the holes in a camera lens that keen photographers adjust.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally gaps or holes, the word is used in photography for the lens opening controlling light.

clue.text: What's normal for street — and a road

explanation.surface: A question about what counts as usual for a street and a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm or usual level against which things are measured is this.

clue.text: Each green tax suffers a conversion factor

indicators.note: suffers suggests the words each green tax are knocked about and rearranged

explanation.surface: Every environmental levy takes a hit.
explanation.definitionFit: The rate at which one currency is turned into another is a multiplier used in money conversion.

clue.text: An argument against time to finish and compete

parts.note: a con is an argument against, as in pros and cons
end means finish

explanation.surface: Someone raises an objection against the clock to conclude a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: To vie or strive against rivals is a synonym of compete.

clue.text: Channels that provide good talks

parts.note: utters means speaks or talks

explanation.surface: TV stations offering worthwhile discussions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channels' suggests television stations; it means the troughs that carry rainwater.
explanation.definitionFit: Troughs along roofs or roadsides that carry water away are drainage channels.

clue.text: One pretends to sit on centre court chair at last

parts.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose

indicators.note: centre takes the middle letter of court
'at last' asks for the final letter of chair

explanation.surface: A show-off on a seat at the middle of a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who behaves affectedly to impress others is a pretender of this kind.

clue.text: Gathering for golf in Europe, perhaps

indicators.note: 'in' places the golf letter inside the larger landmass

parts.note: Europe is an example of a continent, flagged by perhaps
Golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A golfing team assembles somewhere on the Continent.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of people gathered as part of a larger body, such as a delegation, is called this.

clue.text: Cash needed for an enjoyable day?

parts.note: fun as an adjective means enjoyable

explanation.surface: Money is required for a good day out.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserve of money, such as a sum held for a purpose, is a sense of cash.

clue.text: Film of chief engineer

indicators.note: engineer as a verb means to contrive or rework, so the letters of chief are rearranged

explanation.surface: A movie about the top engineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engineer' looks like a noun paired with 'chief'; it is the anagram signal working on CHIEF.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheet of microfilm bearing tiny images of documents is this.

clue.text: Costly, debilitating disease — oh no!

parts.note: dear means expensive or costly
ME is myalgic encephalomyelitis, chronic fatigue syndrome

explanation.surface: An expensive, draining illness prompts a cry of dismay.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of dismay or surprise.

clue.text: Divine ruler backed firm in dire threat

indicators.note: 'in' puts the reversed firm inside the rearranged letters
dire suggests the word threat is in a bad way and so rearranged
backed means the firm's abbreviation is turned backwards

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A heavenly sovereign supported a business facing a grave danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' might suggest a god, but this ruler is human, governing in God's name. 'dire' rearranges the threat into THERAT, 'backed' turns the firm round, and 'in' sets it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who governs in the name of God, ruling by religious authority, is this.

clue.text: Live on the edge?

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in business letters
a side is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A question whether to dwell at the margins.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell or have one's home somewhere is a synonym of live.

clue.text: Rise on hearing a broadcast

indicators.note: 'on hearing' says the letters are those of words as spoken

parts.note: a send is a transmission, a broadcast, here said out loud

explanation.surface: Someone stands up after listening to a radio programme.
explanation.definitionFit: To go up or climb is a synonym of rise.
